A1.justification: Despite the changed title and algorithm names, both PDFs describe the same NMF research, with matching authors, Hessian-majorant construction, and overlapping experiments. All pages, figures, equations, and appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v2 Section 5 reports original synthetic NLS/NMF benchmarks, inner-loop tuning experiments, and MAPS audio and Urban hyperspectral experiments in Figures 1–10.

after.justification: v3 Section 6 reports original synthetic and real-data experiments comparing the proposed algorithms with baselines, including runtime–loss curves in Figures 1–6.

M1.justification: The core fastMU update survives as mSOM/AmSOM, but v3 extends the procedure to β-divergence for β in [1,2], introduces columnwise initialization scaling, and adds an optional MU fallback for nonquadratic updates. Section 5.4 also introduces MUSOM, using the MU preconditioner with an aggressive stepsize. The fallback is explicitly not used in the reported experiments.

E1.justification: The synthetic NLS/NMF, MAPS, and Urban domains remain, but evaluated conditions change substantially. v3 replaces uniform-noise simulations with Gaussian/Poisson cases, removes the two KL scenarios involving direct data sparsification, and substitutes Bach’s first Prelude for the second. Audio/Frobenius and Urban/KL evaluations disappear. No intermediate-β experiments accompany the theoretical extension.

E2.justification: v2 evaluates MU, HALS, NeNMF, and GD for Frobenius, but only MU for KL. v3 adds MUSOM to both loss families and ScalarNewton’s CCD variant to the KL comparisons, with reported curves. GD becoming PGD and the added alternating-method prefixes are naming changes.

E3.justification: v2 uses dynamic inner stopping with δ=0.1; v3 normally fixes 10 inner iterations, with 3 for ASN CCD, and changes initialization and iteration budgets. KL NLS dimensions change from [2000,1000,40] to [200,100,10], while audio rank 176 is replaced by {2,11,23,45}. Lower-SNR cases are added. The right-hand Frobenius rank in v3 Figures 1–2 remains ambiguous: plots label 10, whereas text and captions specify 5.

E4.justification: v2’s explicit stopping-tolerance sweep and inner-iteration analyses in Figures 1–2 are removed. v3 adds MUSOM controls to distinguish the effects of aggressive stepsizes and majorant selection, plus audio rank-sensitivity and failure analyses in Figure 5. Noise and sparsity robustness experiments are also substantially revised.

E5.justification: The reported default synthetic realization count changes from 5 to 100, while the Frobenius NLS exception remains 10. v3 consistently specifies 10 real-data initializations; v2’s prose says 5 but its captions already say 10. Both retain median-curve reporting without confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: v3 adds MUSOM and ScalarNewton results, lower-SNR results, and four audio-rank comparisons, while removing the tuning, audio/Frobenius, and Urban/KL results. New findings include near-equivalence of AmSOM and AMUSOM in several synthetic KL NMF settings and increasing AmSOM loss in the rank-two audio case. Changed data and protocols prevent interpreting these replacement curves as same-setting improvements over v2.

T1.justification: v2 provides stationary-point convergence claims without convergence rates. v3 adds β-divergence derivations, Proposition 3’s claimed Frobenius linear rate, Theorem 5’s local noiseless β-divergence rate, and their Section 4 proofs, while revising KL convergence conditions. Appendix C replaces the existing optimality proof, Appendix B revises the retained min-max proof, and Appendix D adds a scaling proof.

C1.justification: v3 recasts the contribution from a faster MU-related algorithm with unknown convergence speed into a general SOM framework with β-divergence extensions and linear-rate claims. Its abstract also strengthens v2’s qualified speed and competitiveness claims to consistently outperforming state-of-the-art algorithms, although the body and conclusion retain clear exceptions.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly recognizes that its nonquadratic surrogate is not a global loss majorant and distinguishes local noiseless convergence from safeguarded alternating convergence. It develops v2’s brief sparsity and initialization caveats into a basin-of-attraction explanation, discusses loss increases despite careful initialization, and interprets the separate contributions of stepsize and preconditioner.

D1.justification: v3 adds CPU and RAM specifications, explicit precomputation and broadcasting instructions, and details of interpolating timing grids for median curves. The MM-nmf repository and shootout tooling remain. Conversely, v2’s numerical implementation example ε=10^-16 is no longer supplied.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands research positioning around joint NMF optimization, coordinate/Newton methods, mirror/Bregman methods, and extrapolation. New discussions include Marmin et al. (2023), Malitsky and Mishchenko (2020), and Takahashi et al. (2024, 2025), explaining how SOM relates to these approaches beyond the earlier emphasis on MU and forward-backward methods.

P1.justification: The title, terminology, and extensive passages are rewritten. v2’s background, majorant-construction, and fastMU sequence becomes separate Frobenius and β-divergence developments, followed by dedicated convergence-rate and implementation sections. Proofs are reorganized into explicit Appendices A–D, substantially changing the narrative structure.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a JMLR page template with running headers and reformatted algorithm boxes. Benchmark plots are redrawn with revised legends, larger composite displays, and logarithmic time axes in many comparisons. The audio comparison becomes an eight-panel rank display, while the tuning figures and two real-data loss comparisons are removed.

improvement.justification: v3 adds valuable stepsize controls and a stronger KL baseline, and corrects v2’s global-majorization framing for KL. However, its new Proposition 3 claims strict contraction under assumptions that allow rank-deficient W, for which the displayed contraction factor cannot be below one. Its abstract also claims consistent superiority despite the audio exceptions in Figure 5. These material benefits and unresolved theoretical and claim defects prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
